Commentary.Commentary: Is 173 chaseable? Perhaps. No Kuldeep or Chahal on a slow pitch. Too many runs? Time will tell. Stay tuned for the answer...

They say, if you don't begin well, generally it is not a good day for you. Morris overstepped on the very first ball of the match and ended up with figures of 4-0-43-2. The bowling could have been much better had the chances been taken. Junior Dala was impressive once again while Aaron Phangiso strangely bowled only 2 overs.

India lost an early wicket again, this time Rohit Sharma managing more than 0. Dhawan and Raina then got going, managing a 65-run stand for the second wicket, surviving a few chances given by the South Africans. From there on, the Indian innings lost momentum. They got the odd boundary here and there but concentrated on the running.
Not a bad total by India but 47/4 in the last 5 overs - that might just hurt them. However, on a slower deck, 173 might just be a bit too much for the Proteas.
A yorker outside off, Axar dabs it towards mid off and the batsmen take a run. 10 from the over, with 2 wickets as well. INDIA FINISH ON 172/7!

Full on middle, flicked straight to square leg. Andile Phehlukwayo misfields and the ball nearly runs to the fence but Junior Dala rushes to his right from mid-wicket in the deep and saves the boundary. Three runs taken.
Bhuvneshwar Kumar walks in now.

OUT! Well, he gets in a wicket now. The second of the over. Karthik walks across his stumps and misses his flick. The ball is straight and he is hit on his back foot. He takes the review after the umpire gives it out but starts to walk any which ways. Hawk Eye shows the impact to be in line and hitting the stumps.
LBW! But Karthik has taken the review. But he is walking back anyways...
WIDE. Third from Morris tonight. This is down the leg side again.
FOUR! Poor ball, full and down the leg side, Karthik flicks it to the fine leg fence.
Axar Patel walks in now.

OUT! Pandya is gone. Big blow. Another slower ball, on middle and leg, Pandya is way too early into his flick but gets a leading edge. The ball goes miles in the air and three men come into contention - point, the keeper and short third man. Actually only two because it is Tabraiz Shamsi at short third man who does not move a muscle. Heinrich Klaasen calls for it and takes it calmly.
Follows the batsman down the leg side, Karthik looks to play the reverse sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. A leg bye taken. Morris and Karthik smile.
Chris Morris to bowl the final over. 180? 185? Here we go...
A short ball, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a run. 11 from the over.
FOUR! Easy peasy. Making use of the field. Mid off is up and Karthik goes up and over. One bounce and into the fence.
FOUR! Stunning shot. On a length outside off, Karthik waits for the ball to come to him and steers it behind point for a boundary!
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
WIDE. Miles outside off, left alone.
Dinesh Karthik finally gets a chance to bat.

OUT! Dhoni holes out. He smiles. Very rarely does one see Dhoni getting caught at the boundary, that too down the ground. A length ball outside off, Dhoni looks to go over the top and seems to hit it pretty well too. But does not have the distance. David Miller takes it with ease at long off.
FOUR! Streaky! On a length outside off, Dhoni looks to push through the off side but gets a thick inside edge which goes past the stumps and beats short fine leg!
Junior Dala time.
The batsman has worked it off his pads behind square. They pick up a single.
A short ball, around off, Dhoni looks to pull but the ball goes over his head. Dhoni asks the square leg umpire about the wide but gets a negative answer.
Driven towards the mid on region. They pick up a single.
SIX! STUPENDOUS! A boundary after 29 balls! What a way to get that too. A length ball, around off, Pandya just pushes it over mid on and it goes all the way!
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
On middle, Dhoni pushes it towards long on, calls for two and gets them with ease.
Chris Morris is back on.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single. Just 6 from that over - only 19 from the last 3.
Chips this towards long on and gets a run.
A slower ball, outside off, Hardik looks to punch but gets a bottom edge back to the bowler.

Down the leg side, Hardik pushes it through mid-wicket and calls for two. Dhoni is so quick that even before Farhaan Behardien gets to the ball, the second is completed. The facial expression of Farhaan says it all.
Pushes this down to mid on for a run.
Full and outside off, pushed towards long off for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed to the off side for another one. 5 runs and a run out from that over. Shamsi finishes with figures of 4-0-31-1.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, pushed through mid off for a run.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot for a single.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Mahendra Singh Dhoni walks in now, for the finishing duties. This is mouthwatering stuff. Two death over specialists in the middle.

OUT! Well, Dhawan is walking but we are not sure whether that is out. On description of the ball, Dhawan comes down the track and whips it through mid-wicket. Hardik always wanted two and because he took a start, it helps him. But Dhawan takes a bit longer and hence is gone for all money. Junior Dala returns a superb throw to Heinrich Klaasen at the stumps and the LED illuminates. Dhawan starts to go but the umpire wants to check - did Klaasen disturb the bails before the ball hit the timber? Does anyone care? Certainly not Gabbar. He is off. Could have waited a bit longer for the third umpire's decision.
Direct hit? Or has Klassen taken the bails off? Dhawan is already walking off without even waiting for the confirmation. But the umpire has signalled it upstairs.
Driven towards the mid on region. The batsmen have run through for a single.

WIDE. A mega wide. Just as we have popcorn options in a multiplex cinema - Regular, Large and Tub - we should also have something for wides. This would have fallen in the third category. Phehlukwayo attempts a slower delivery but it goes horribly wrong, bowling it outside the pitch. Dhawan thinks about the paddle but then lets it go.
A short ball, at the head of the batsman, Pandya plays that nicely, keeping the bat over the ball and controlling the pull shot, all along the ground, towards deep mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full on middle, Hardik chips it uppishly but it goes wide of the diving Andile.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They manage to come back for the second.
Full and outside off, chipped through the air wide of mid off for a couple.

WIDE. Pandya gets across his stumps and Phehlukwayo bowls it around leg stump. The ball goes down with the angle and Hardik misses his flick. A bowler might argue that it should not have been a wide. A batsman might say, well, it was down the leg side. What should the umpire do? Goes with the batsman in this case.
Andile Phehlukwayo is brought back on as well.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a run.
A short delivery which has been pulled away. They pick up a single.
Outside off, nips back in, Pandya is late in his defense and gets hit on the pads. The ball rolls to the off side and the batsmen pinch a single. No signal, so an inside edge must have been there.
The batsman has driven it through mid off. They pick up a single.

Outside off, punched through the covers. The throw comes in to Dala as the batsman pinch a second but the bowler misfields and it goes all the way down to long on. Hardik wants the third but Dhawan has backed up too far, hence is not aware. The angry young man gets angry again. The other day he was disappointed with one of the fielders when he conceded the second run off his bowling.
Hardik Pandya walks in at number 5, replacing Pandey.

OUT! It is a catch and since it is not Shamsi, it is not down. Dala immediately strikes on return. He lands it on a length outside off, it cuts back in, Pandey looks to help it to the leg side but the ball skids through. Beats Pandey who can only get a top edge. He does not even want to run, so disappointed is he with that shot. Still, to give Dhawan the strike, he crosses over. Knows what is going to be the end result. It is David Miller underneath the ball at long on. Another failure for Pandey.
Change of pace. Junior Dala replaces Shamsi.
Full and outside off,  driven towards long off for one more. 9 runs from that over, but poor Phangiso could have had a wicket.
Full again, outside off, slogged towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! SLAUGHTERED! Pay the price now. Full and outside off, Dhawan dances out and hits it over mid off for a boundary!

TOP EDGE, MISSED AGAIN! Guess who is the fielder? Tabraiz Shamsi. Oh dear... fielding is not in his agenda. Full and outside off, Shikhar looks to sweep but gets a top edge. The ball goes miles in the air and Shamsi at short fine leg should have gobbled it. Instead, the opportunity presents a nervousness which gobbles him. He stutters and misses the ball. Two runs taken.
Quicker one now. Outside off, a bit short, Dhawan looks to cut but the ball skids through, staying low and beats him.
Tossed up outside off, a bit slow, Pandey comes down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball, waits for it to come and blasts it to long on for a single.
FOUR! That is rubbish. Short and outside off, pulled to the deep mid-wicket fence.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Comes down the track and eases it to long off for a single.
FOUR! First boundary for Dhawan! On his 29th ball. A short ball, around off, Dhawan gets down and pull-sweeps it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Drives this through mid on for a run.

SIX! Total misjudgement from the fielder! David Miller is the culprit. That should have been taken. Full and outside off, Pandey gets down and smites it over long on. Should have been taken but for some reason, David Miller comes running in and the ball goes beyond his head. Clears the ropes but he would have taken it had been at the fence.
Looks to flick but the ball goes off the inner half through mid-wicket. No signal, must have been an inside edge. Just 4 from the opening over for Phangiso.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Comes down the track again, takes it on the full and drives it to long off for one.
Dropped? Nope. Crowd catch. Full on middle, Shikhar comes down the track and hits it straight back to Phangiso who cannot hold on. Replays show that it came to him on the bounce.
Full and wide outside off, Pandey stays leg side of the ball and drives it through the covers for a run.
Full on leg stump, eased to long on for a single.
Aaron Phangiso gets a look-in now.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Flicks it through the leg side to get going, Pandey.
Manish Pandey is the new man in, replacing Raina.

OUT! Got him! Good running catch at long on! A wicket at the right time for South Africa! Shamsi loops it up around middle and off, Raina gets down on one knee and tries to hit it down the ground. Made good connection and it seemed like a biggie but... Farhaan Behardien comes across to his right from long on and takes a superb catch just near the rope. He covered it up for his misfield in a stunning manner.
Gets down to sweep but gets it off the inside edge towards square leg for a single.
Floated ball around middle, SD gets into the position early and reverse sweeps it over cover-point for a couple of runs.
Chance of a run out! Raina works it towards the left of the bowler and sets off for a single. Shamsi gets to the ball but doesn't collect it which allows Raina to make his way back.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. One run added to the total.
Loopy ball outside off, Raina comes down the track and drives it along the ground towards wide long off for a couple.

FOUR! Behardien eases off the pressure that his side had built! Short ball, quicker through the air outside off, Raina goes back and punches it towards cover where Farhaan fails to stop it and lets it through his fingers for a boundary. FB apologizes immediately.
Jumps out of the track and drives it to long on for another single.
Darts it with a round-arm action, SR makes room and punches it to sweeper cover for a single.
Slower through the air, around off, Shikhar gets down on one knee and pulls it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Eases it past the man this time and scampers to the other end. A good start from chinaman, just 3 off his first over.
Floated ball outside off, Dhawan isn't to the pitch of the ball and hence mistimes the drive to cover.
Goes back to a shorter ball and punches it through cover for one. Brings up the 50-run stand between the two as well.
Very full, fires on off, jammed back to Tabriaz.
Loops it up around middle, Raina looks to flick it away but misses and gets hit on the pads. A loud appeal but the umpire turns it down.
Starts off with a flatter delivery around the pads, Dhawan flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Tabraiz Shamsi is brought on to bowl now.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.

Inside edge saves Dhawan! Shikhar comes dancing down the track to hit it across the line but is done in in the flight. Gets a lucky inside edge which hits his pads and rolls past the keeper to fine leg for a brace.
Duminy sees Dhawan giving the charge and hence he drags his length back. Shikhar could only punch it back to the bowler.
Flatter ball outside off, Suresh Raina punches it towards cover for an easy single.
Fuller outside off, broomed behind square on the leg side for a single.
Floated delivery around middle, Raina looks to slog but misses and wears it on the pads.
JP Duminy is back into the attack.
Dabs it towards Shamsi at short third man and sets off. The spinner has a shy at the striker's end but misses. 10 from the over, India end with 57/1 in the Powerplay!
Eases the fuller ball down to long on for one.

In and out of Shamsi's hands! Sigh! Catches don't come that easy, I tell you! On a length and closer to the off stump line. Dhawan doesn't have any room to cut but he still goes on with the shot. Ekes out a thickish edge straight towards Tabraiz Shamsi at short third man who spills it out. They still take a single. Will this be a costly drop?
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
FOUR! That's a good shot! On a shorter length outside off, Raina stays leg side and opens the bat face to get it uppushly through point. Shamsi at third man can't get to it. A boundary results.
Morris from around the wicket, hits it on a back of a length outside off, SR tries fetching it from outside off, gets it off the inner half down to fine leg for a brace.
Chris Morris to bowl the last over of the Powerplay.

Nearly chops it on! Makes room does Raina, Phehlukwayo follows him, Suresh dabs it off the off stump towards point and gets to the other end. The fielder has a wild shy at the non-striker's end but misses.
Fuller ball, angling in on the pads, worked towards Duminy at mid on.
Wide! Tries the slower delivery, wider outside off, Raina doesn't play at it.
On a length and outside off, Dhawan looks to pull but gets it off the inner half towards mid-wicket for one.
Now flicks it through square leg and gets to the other end. Dhawan wanted another one but there was never a second there.
FOUR! Beautiful! Raina has moved to 22 in 10 balls. Half volley on off, Suresh Raina presses forward and delightfully hit it through cover. Pierces the gap and fetches himself another boundary.
FOUR! What a shot! Andile is welcomed in some style. He delivers a length ball outside off, Raina dances down the track and lofts it over mid off to start the over with a boundary.
Andile Phehlukwayo is brought into the attack.
Dhawan presses forward and strokes it straight to the man at cover.
Ahead of a length outside off, Shikhar swings across the line. Didn't time it well and hence the ball stops near the deep mid-wicket area. Another brace added to the total.
Good shot! On a length and outside off, Dhawan cracks it through point. The fielder gives it a chase and does well to pull the ball back in play. Two taken.
Slants it away on a length outside off, Dhawan goes chasing after it but fails to get any bat on it.
Length ball, strangling down leg, pulled to fine leg but for just a single.
On a length and outside off, punched from the crease towards cover.
Raina gets down to sweep but misses to get it off the pads towards point for a leg bye. 8 from the first over of Duminy.
Floated ball outside off, driven down to long off for a single.
The batsman has driven it straight down the ground.
Tossed up around middle and leg, clipped through square leg for one.
FOUR! Dropped short outside off, Raina camps back and punches it through extra cover for another boundary. He has got a good start here.
Flicked away through mid-wicket for a single.
JP Duminy to roll his arm over.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. 9 runs and a wicket off it.
Angling away from a length outside off, Suresh drives it on the up through cover and collects a brace.

SIX! That has gone the distance! Any batsman would love to get a ball there to get off the mark. Fuller ball down the leg side, Raina walks across a touch and dumps it over deep backward square leg for a maximum to open his tally.
Suresh Raina is the new man in at no. 3.

OUT! Dala removes Rohit for the third time! Start all the bunny talks now. Junior drops it on a length around middle, it skids a bit off the deck and stays a touch low too. Rohit is late to bring his bat down this time and wears it on the pads. A loud appeal follows to which the umpire raises the finger after a thought. Dhawan wanted to have a chat but Rohit wasn't interested. The umpire however, wants to have a check at the front foot. It is completely fine and Sharma is asked to walk away. Replays show that it seemed to be missing the leg. Almost a carbon copy of his dismissal at SuperSport Park.
Rolls his finger on the ball, hurls it on a length around middle and off, Rohit hangs back in defense.
Starts his spell with a fuller delivery on off, Dhawan gets it off the inner half towards mid on for a single.
Junior Dala will bowl from the other end. He has been really good so far. Can he emulate even today?

FOUR! That's a horror delivery from Morris! It had to be put away and Rohit obliges. Length delivery, down the leg side, Rohit just helps it on its way towards fine leg to pick up back-to-back boundaries.
FOUR! Caressed! Morris overpitches it by a margin, Rohit nicely brings his bat down and just times it down the ground. Nothing mid on fielder could do about it. First boundary of the match.
Curling back in on middle, Sharma clips it towards square leg. Wants a single but won't get it.
On a length and nipping back in a shade, Rohit stands back and defends it in the direction of the bowler.
Keeps it full and serves it around off, Dhawan leans ahead to drive but mistimes it towards mid off. The man is a bit deep there which allows the southpaw to open his account.
Gets away with that! Full toss, wider outside off, Rohit Sharma goes after it but gets it off the toe-end of the bat through cover for just a single.
Free Hit coming up...
Have I jinxed him? Morris starts off with a huge front foot no ball. Fuller in length and angling back in on the pads, clipped easily away down to fine leg for a couple of runs.

Time for the national anthems then. It will be India's first followed by South Africa's. After the completion of it we are all set to get underway. The players and umpires are walking in the middle. There is a South African team huddle near the boundary rope. Now come the Indian openers - Rohit Sharma and Shikhar Dhawan. It will be Chris Morris to steam in first up. A couple of slips in place. He bowled a maiden in the previous T20I. Can he start well again?

India skipper, Rohit Sharma informs Kohli has got a stiff back which is why he misses out today and Dinesh Karthik replaces him. Adds Axar Patel and Jasprit Bumrah replace Yuzvendra Chahal and Jaydev Unadkat. States in the last two games they have done decently with the bat and knows where did they go wrong. Is hoping that they end the tour on a high with a win. Reckons it looks a good batting wicket and feels that it should remain the same for the full 40 overs. Is excited for the decider and wants to put up a good show so that the crowd gets entertained as they have been coming in numbers to support them.

Protea skipper, JP Duminy says chasing has been the formula that has worked for them and hence they don't want to change it. Further says the wicket looks good with a fair bit of grass covering on it that should help his bowlers in the first six overs. Informs about the two changes that they have got for this game - JJ Smuts and Dane Paterson will miss out and Christiaan Jonker (debut) and Aaron Phangiso come in. Also, tells us that David Miller will open the batting tonight and he hopes that they do the basics right.

Toss - As expected, the Indians have not taken risk with Kohli who isn't fit. Rohit Sharma is out for the toss alongside JP Duminy. The former calls it wrong and it will be South Africa bowling for the THIRD TIME on the trot in the series.

South Africa, on the other hand, will be brimming with confidence after their stunning win in the second T20I. Heinrich Klaasen and JP Duminy have looked in good touch and they would hope to rub the same on others too. Their openers have struggled big time but given that they have won the last game and with momentum firmly on their side, it's highly unlikely that they would tweak the playing XI. Still we shall wait and find out as Shaun Pollock is out with the two skippers for the toss.

It all boils down the to the 'decider' in Cape Town today. Are you ready? We welcome you to the coverage of the final game on this long Indian tour to South Africa. First and foremost, Virat Kohli isn't deemed fit and is likely to miss out today. It would be interesting to see who fills in for him. Overall, the Indians have been good in limited-overs cricket and now it's time to put the right foot forward. Another good show and they will get their hands on the trophy but mind you, it won't be that easy.
